question.text: Suppose the family of lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> (where <math><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></math> are in arithmetic progression) be normal to a family of circles. The radius of the circle of the family which intersects the circle <math><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> orthogonally is

solution.text:
Since, a,b,c are in A.P

ax+by+c=0 represents a family of lines passing through the point 1,-2.

So, the family of circles (concentric) will be given by x2+y2-2x+4y+c=0 and

2-1×-2+2×-2=-1+c⇒c=-3

⇒radius=1+4+3=22 units
